g.text: The transfer coordinator writes its INTENT before it acts
Without that record, a crash after the debit leaves an orphaned debit that nothing knows to compensate.
NOT a rollback. The Debited event
stays in the log FOREVER and a new
it - so the audit trail shows what

The leg times out. Do you compensate?
assume it FAILED, compensate the debit
-> if the credit actually succeeded, you credit back
money that was never removed. A MINT.
-> if it actually failed, the recipient was credited
without the sender being debited. ALSO A MINT.
-> a recovery worker resolves it by READING
applied_legs on the partition. The only safe move.
On timeout the coordinator does NOT know whether the leg applied - the request may have committed and the response been lost.
This is why partitions expose idempotency on (transaction_id, leg_number) rather than the coordinator merely tracking its own
attempts: the coordinator's memory of what it did is not trustworthy. The log is.
Read path - zero consensus, zero coordination
This path is why balance queries can be orders of magnitude more frequent than transfers
without touching the write path at all. as_of_sequence exposes the consistency boundary
rather than hiding it - a bare balance is ambiguous, because the client cannot tell whether
it reflects the transfer they just made.
follower dies Raft continues on quorum. No impact.
LEADER dies new leader in seconds; replays its log tail
partition loses quorum WRITES STOP. Deliberate: accepting writes
without quorum risks losing acknowledged money.
coordinator dies recovery workers pick up stuck transfers.
read models fail queries degrade; TRANSFERS CONTINUE.
That last line is the nice property of CQRS: the read side is fully expendable.
